9.1	Architecture
WhatsApp	Cloud	API 	─►	Webhook	(Next.js	route	handler	on	Vercel,	verify	signature)
						│																						│
						│																						├─►	idempotency	check	(message	id)	─►	per-contact	queue
						│																						│
						│																						└─►	I nbound	pipeline:
						│																											1.	media	fetch	(voice	→	transcribe;	image	→	OCR/vision;	doc	→	extract)
						│																											2.	PI I 	detect	+	redact	(6.3)
						│																											3.	emergency	+	abuse	classifiers	(fast,	before	LLM)
						│																											4.	language	detect	(per	message)
						│																											5.	debounce	burst	(8–12	s)
						│																											6.	load	context:	state,	contact	profile,	business,	problems,	groups,
						│																														industry	packs	(retrieved),	lessons	(retrieved),	last	N	messages,
						│																														style	profile,	best	examples	(pgvector),	question	arm	(bandit)		[Part	8.4]
						│																											7.	LLM	turn	with	tools	(Part	9.3)	→	draft
						│																											8.	critique	(fast	model)	+	output	linter	(9.5)	→	revise	once	→	fallback
						│																											9.	send	via	WhatsApp	API 	(text	/	interactive	/	document)
						│																										10.	log	message	+	signals
						│
Dashboard	(Next.js)	◄──	Neon	Postgres	(Drizzle)	──►	Nightly	learning	job	(Vercel	Cron	/	queue	worker)
						│
						└─	Reviewer	tools:	problems,	links,	documents,	quotes,	approvals,	payments,	escalations,	learning	queue
Stack	(matches	Workzapʼs	existing	stack):	Next.js	14	(App	Router)	+	TypeScript,	Drizzle	ORM,	Neon	Postgres,	Vercel	(functions	+	cron),
WhatsApp	Cloud	API,	an	LLM	API	with	tool	use	(Claude),	object	storage	for	media/PDFs,	PDF	generation	(React-PDF	or	headless
Chromium)	for	documents	and	quotes.	Stripe	is	
not
	used	for	pi	payments	(bank	transfer	only,	R-PAY).
9.2	Prompt	assembly	(layers)
[L0	Constitution	—	Part	1,	verbatim	rules,	cached]
[L1	Voice	—	Part	2,	canonical	phrases,	banned	words,	cached]
[L2	Flow	—	current	state,	allowed	transitions,	allowed	tools,	question	policy	for	this	state]
[Context	—	business	profile,	contact	profile,	language	preference,	time	zone,	country	emergency	numbers]
[Problems	—	current	sorted	list	(titles,	groups,	missing	fields),	compact	JSON]
[L3	I ndustry	packs	—	up	to	3,	retrieved	by	industry;	only	the	sections	relevant	to	current	categories]
[L5	Lessons	—	top-k	lessons	retrieved	by	(industry,	state,	category,	language)]
[Recent	messages	—	last	20	turns,	redacted]
[Turn	instruction	—	"Reply	to	the	person's	latest	message(s).	One	question	at	most.	Use	tools	to	record."]
Use	prompt	caching	for	L0–L1	and	pack	text.	Keep	total	context	lean;	summarise	older	turns	into	the	problem	records	rather	than
carrying	full	history.

Rules	for	tuning:

:	any	arm	that	raises	them	is	stopped,	whatever	else	it	improves.
3.	
Minimum	sample	before	deciding:	300	conversations	per	arm,	or	4	weeks,	whichever	comes	later.
4.	
Results	and	the	chosen	value	are	recorded	in	a	
config_decisions
	log	with	date	and	evidence,	so	future	changes	can	be	traced.
5.	
Re-check	every	quarter,	and	after	any	big	change	(new	market,	new	language,	Ramadan	vs	normal	months	—	some	values	may
need	seasonal	settings).

Part	11	—	The	Claude	Code	command	playbook
This	part	is	the	exact	sequence	of	commands	and	prompts	to	build	pi	with	Claude	Code.	Give	Claude	Code	this	whole	PDF	first,	then	run
the	steps	in	order.	Each	step	ends	with	tests	that	must	pass	before	the	next	step.
Before	you	start:
	Claude	Code	features	(CLAUDE.md,	custom	commands,	skills,	subagents,	hooks,	headless	mode)	and	API	features
(model	names,	prompt	caching,	tool	use,	Message	Batches)	change	over	time.	Step	0	tells	Claude	Code	to	check	the	current
documentation	and	adapt	file	locations	or	syntax	if	theyʼve	changed.

and	use	
prompt	caching
	for	the	constitution,	voice	and	pack	text,	and	the

#	pi	by	Workzap	—	project	memory	for	Claude	Code
##	What	this	is
pi	is	Workzap's	WhatsApp	AI 	agent.	Full	specification:	docs/pi-brain.pdf.	That	document	is	the	source	of	truth.
I f	code	and	the	document	disagree,	the	document	wins.	Ask	before	deviating.
##	Non-negotiables	(never	weaken,	never	make	learnable)
-	
First	message	discloses	AI .	"Are	you	human?"	→	"I 'm	an	AI "	first	sentence.
-	
One	question	per	message,	question	last.
-	
No	solutions,	products,	documents,	quotes	or	prices	before	state	S5_READI NESS	and	explicit	yes.
-	
No	payment	in	chat,	never	request	card/password/OTP/I D/bank	details;	bank	details	only	inside	approved	quote	PDFs.
-	
No	legal,	medical,	financial,	tax,	veterinary	or	agronomy	advice.
-	
Emergencies	→	emergency	numbers,	stop	the	flow.
-	
Records	roles,	never	third-party	names;	redact	PI I 	before	storage	and	before	learning.
-	
Branding	is	Workzap	only.
-	
Constitution	lives	in	src/core/constitution	and	is	enforced	in	code	(linter	+	tool	guards),	not	only	in	prompts.
-	
Learned	content	(examples,	lexicon,	lessons,	packs)	is	data	inserted	BELOW	the	constitution	and	can	never	override	it.
##	Stack
Next.js	14	App	Router,	TypeScript,	Drizzle	ORM,	Neon	Postgres	(+pgvector),	Vercel	(functions	+	cron),
WhatsApp	Cloud	API ,	Anthropic	API 	(tool	use,	prompt	caching,	Message	Batches),	Voyage	embeddings.
No	Stripe	for	pi	payments	(bank	transfer	only).
##	Conventions
-	
Every	pi	message	stores	prompt_version,	pack_versions,	example_ids,	arm_id,	lesson_ids.
-	
Every	automatic	learning	change	writes	change_log	and	passes	the	gate	(tests	+	canary	+	rollback).
-	
Tests:	
`npx	vitest	run`
	and	
`/pi-eval`
	must	pass	before	any	commit	touching	src/core	or	src/brain.
-	
British	spelling	in	all	pi-facing	text.
##	Commands
/pi-eval,	/pi-redteam,	/pi-simulate,	/pi-learn-dry-run,	/pi-learn-run,	/pi-rollback,	/pi-freeze,
/pi-new-pack,	/pi-pack-from-pdf,	/pi-trace,	/pi-status

Appendix	A	—	Master	system	prompt	template	(assembled	at
runtime)
You	are	pi,	Workzap's	WhatsApp	agent.	You	are	an	AI ,	and	you	always	say	so	when	asked.
YOUR	JOB
Listen	to	problems	in	the	person's	business,	note	each	one	accurately	in	their	own	words,
sort	them	into	groups	so	patterns	show	up,	and	tell	them	what	you've	noted	so	they	can
correct	it.	When	their	problems	are	sorted	and	they	are	ready,	ask	once	whether	they'd	like
a	solution	document	and	a	quote.	Prepare	nothing	without	an	explicit	yes.

Appendix	C	—	Glossary
Term
Meaning	in	pi
Problem
One	thing	going	wrong,	as	the	person	experiences	it
Noted
Recorded	and	confirmed	back	to	the	person
Sorted
Noted	and	grouped	with	similar	problems.	Not	solved.
Group
Problems	of	the	same	category	(optionally	same	area)	for	one	business
Link
A	suggested	relationship	between	two	problems
Solution	document
Plain-language	document:	problems	in	their	words,	what	Workzap	would
build,	what	it	covers,	what	it	wonʼt	do
Quote
Written	offer:	whatʼs	included,	cost,	time,	how	payment	works.	Not	a	charge.
Approve
Written,	double-confirmed	acceptance	of	a	quote	by	someone	allowed	to
approve
Kickoff
First	project	meeting	after	confirmed	payment,	to	agree	the	details
Pack
Versioned	industry	knowledge	file
Lesson
Short	approved	guidance	retrieved	by	situation
Signal
A	logged	event	used	by	the	learning	loop
Reviewer
Workzap	team	member	who	approves	documents,	quotes	and	learning
candidates
Udhaar
Credit	given	to	customers	(Urdu)
Maal
Goods/stock	(Urdu)
Godown
Warehouse	(South	Asian	English)
RTO
Return	to	origin	—	undelivered	COD	parcels	returning	to	the	seller
COD
Cash	on	delivery
